thread:
maya: Heads-up — ran into a weird streaming glitch during mobile onboarding. iOS app backgrounded, then resumed, and the SDK delivered a duplicated tail fragment that looked like a complete final chunk. App tried to parse and crashed.

sam: ugh. which SDK version? any repro steps?

maya: using ios-sdk v1.4.2 (the sample onboarding flow). Steps: open chat demo, lock phone, wait ~30s, unlock. Sometimes on resume the UI shows an extra ']' and JSON parse error in the message handler.

jon: that sounds like a fragment boundary got replayed or the client replayed buffered data on reconnect. Do we use last-event-id or resume token on mobile?

maya: mobile keeps a small resume token but we don't send last-event-id over the reconnect path — the SDK currently tries to rehydrate the stream from a queued buffer.

irene: is it consistently duplicated (same bytes) or partial overlap? screenshots/log below: 

maya: paste of logs: 
```
[stream] onpause -> backgrounding
[network] reconnect scheduled (backoff 0.6s)
[stream] resume -> reattach, resume_token=abc123
[parse] received fragment: `{"role":"assistant","content":"render...` (partial)
[parse] received fragment: `tion"}]` (final)
[parse] received fragment (duplicate tail): `}]`  <-- causes parser to think there's an extra object
```

sam: hmm duplicate tail only — suggests we flush buffer after first final chunk but then the reconnect handler replays buffer tail again. Could be our circular buffer pointer off by one when backgrounding race occurs.

alex: which transport on iOS? NSURLSession SSE? Are we doing any keepalive pings on background?

maya: NSURLSession background tasks paused. No keepalives while suspended. On resume we re-open the SSE connection and replay anything in the in-memory buffer.

jon: repro idea: reproduce on simulator, attach lldb and breakpoint in buffer flush code. If we can catch the double-flush we'll know whether it's client-side.

irene: also verify server didn't retransmit final chunk — maybe gateway retried and we got the final data twice (before and after auth refresh). Any gateway logs?

maya: I checked hosted logs for the session id and only one final transmit from upstream; timestamps align that server sent final chunk before client-first-ack. So client is likely duping.

sam: OK. preliminary diagnosis: race between backgrounding -> buffer flush -> reconnect replay. Fix options: 1) make buffer replay idempotent (track last-emitted sequence id and drop duplicates), 2) change resume to send last-event-id and let server decide dedup, or 3) make buffer clearing synchronous before reconnect.

alex: option 2 is nice but needs server support for last-event-id handling — do we have that on hosted?

irene: server can accept last-event-id for some flows but not all model endpoints. Making the client idempotent is safer for cross-deployment parity.

jon: agree. client-side dedupe by sequence token is easiest to roll out quickly in mobile SDK. Also add a debug flag to log fragment seqs to repro.

maya: i'll try a client patch: attach incremental sequence number to fragments in buffer and drop if seq <= lastProcessed. Will test by backgrounding a lot.

sam: also add a unit test for background/resume cycle that simulates partial-delivery + duplicate-tail. Keep it small and flaky-resistant.

maya: noted. if anyone wants to pair on lldb repro tomorrow ping me. I'll also open a minimal PR with the dedupe guard.

bot-deploy: Reminder: when you push sdk changes, run the cross-sdk integration matrix (ios, android, web) — two failing permutations block canary deploys.

irene: nits — put a short note in the onboarding guide about mobile backgrounding and that older SDKs may drop fragments. Helps support triage.

maya: will do. thanks team :thumbsup:
